operational-example.copy: Use Card Summary as a single-card snapshot: identity, masked number, visible status, and one or two local metrics. Wallet carousels, lifecycle actions, and card detail flows remain patterns.

scenario.title: Card Summary
scenario.meta: Single payment-card snapshot informed by the ZIP PaymentCard and CardCompact references, governed by Flow components and tokens.
rationale: The ZIP PaymentCard reference drives the default anatomy: fixed card ratio, top label/status, chip/contactless zone, masked number with expiry, and holder metadata.
CardCompact informs only the compact row variant; it is not the default visual model.
Balance, limit, wallet carousel, quick actions, and card detail flows remain outside the default card summary and escalate to limit variant or patterns.

items.rule: One card-level container for a single payment instrument.
Card name, driver, or vehicle context.
Displays safe card identifier without sensitive data.
Shows active, frozen, warning, or disabled state.
Shows one or two summary values only.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, frozen, warning, active, focus, hover, default
items: Provide a visible accessible label for the component.
Expose status and state in text, not color alone.
Keep keyboard focus and touch targets predictable.
Protect sensitive or operational data from overexposure.
Escalate to a pattern when actions, grouping, or detail flows exceed one component.

variants.copy: Card Summary variants change the emphasis of one payment instrument without adding wallet behavior.

states.copy: Card Summary states expose status through Badge text and Flow state styling; they do not trigger card-management actions.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant controls which card facts are emphasized; state controls availability without adding actions or processs.

full-width.copy: Card Summary can fill mobile sheets and detail headers while staying a single-card summary.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Use compact density on phones, but move control clusters and lifecycle actions to card-detail patterns.

viewport-organization.copy: Viewport rules decide density and metric visibility; they do not add wallet navigation or card management.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use touch-safe targets and preserve key text.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Keep the component close to its related card or movement context.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use compact density only when scanability remains intact.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify masked number, status, variant, state, and summary metrics for one card.

api-foundations.copy: Card Summary API exposes label, metadata, masked number, status, metrics, variant, state, density, and icon while Flow owns visual composition and privacy boundaries.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not include card lifecycle actions inside the component.

items: Check status contrast and non-color cues.

Multiple cards are managed inside one component.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Card Summary as one safe payment-card snapshot. It can choose physical, virtual, compact, or limit emphasis, but must escalate wallet controls and card lifecycle actions to patterns.
canDecide: Use Card Summary for wallet header, driver card preview, admin card row expansion, or mobile card sheet header.
Keep identifiers masked and metrics limited to one or two values.
Use frozen or warning state only with visible copy.
mustAsk: The card surface needs lifecycle actions, support, dispute, replacement, or spending controls.
Sensitive card data, compliance copy, or account ownership is unclear.
Multiple cards need comparison or wallet-level behavior.
rejectIf: Card Summary owns freeze, replace, dispute, or wallet flows.
Multiple cards are managed inside one component.
miel.handoff: I am using Card Summary for one card snapshot. Please confirm masking, status copy, visible metrics, privacy constraints, and whether actions should move to a card-detail pattern.
